newsitem.title: FRANCE: CIC says 1996 profit to rise as expected.
newsitem.headline: CIC says 1996 profit to rise as expected.

text.p: French regional banking group CIC, soon to be privatised, said on Tuesday its second-half results were unlikely to match those of the first half but that it expected a marked rise in full-year profits, in line with expectations.

"In a still uncertain economic context, current business trends and continued productivity and risk control efforts should allow for a marked increase in the 1996 net consolidated result as a whole versus 1995, in line with expectations," the group said in a results statement.
It announced a first half net attributable profit up 60.7 percent at 533 million francs from 332 million in the first half of 1995.
Chairman Bernard Yoncourt told a news conference first-half results were always stronger than those of the second half.
